 The thickness of the elements in a structural region can be defined by setting the parameter T. If no thickness is given, it will be set to a constant value of 1.0 m. In addition to a constant distribution of the thickness, SOFiMSHC also allows to define varying thicknesses within a region. Therefor two possibilities exist:
 • Thickness at boundary edges in record SARB: By setting the thickness value at the outer boundary edges of a region, a varying thickness can be defined.
 • Thickness at structural points within the region: For this, structural points with thickness properties (SPT ... T) can be defined within or on the boundary of the region in order to describe a variable thickness distribution. Since one of these points may be shared by multiple structural regions, the region thickness value at SAR must be set explicitly to T=0.0 in order to activate this setting. Only structural points with no additional geometric information like column sizes etc. will be considered in calculating the thickness distribution.
 In both cases a least square method is applied, which interpolates the thickness values at the support points or lines. In most cases this interpolation reduces to a planar distribution of the thickness values across the region, but may also be higher polynomial in the case that a higher number of support points is given.
 Different stiffnesses in different local directions can be defined by setting orthotroptic thick- ness values (TX, TY, TXY, TD). An average thickness T should be given which will is used for calculating masses etc.
 Meshing of the region can be controlled using a general parameter and different density values. By setting MCTL=REGM SOFiMSHC tries to create a regular (structured) mesh on structural regions with 4 boundary edges. The structured mesh is created as long as the ratio of edges and angles corresponds approximately to a rectangular shape. By default, a unstructured mesh consisting of quadrilateral or triangular elements is created. The parameter H1 sets the element size within the region overwriting the global setting in CTRL HMIN. The value given at H1 defines the maximum length of an element edge. Additionally, H2 can be set to create refinements around structural points inside the region.

By default, a unstructured mesh consisting of quadrilateral or triangular elements is created. The parameter H1 sets the element size within the region overwriting the global setting in CTRL HMIN. The value given at H1 defines the maximum length of an element edge. Additionally, H2 can be set to create refinements around structural points inside the region..
 By setting MCTL=SNGQ the structural region will be converted into a single quad element. The region should have a triangular or quadrilateral structure. This option is useful for defining load distribution areas whose stiffness is deactivated using NRA=0. Since no nodes are created in the interior of the region, problems with large deflections might not occur.
 Option XFLG allows to prevent the automatic intersection of the given structural region with other structural elements. The following options are provided, which can also be combined:
 • ’P’ Structural points will no longer be automatically added as constraining points to the region.
 • ’L’ Other structural lines will no longer be automatically added as constraining lines to the region.
 • ’A’ The structural region will not be intersected with other structural regions. I.e. no inter- section lines will be created automatically. Two structural regions can be placed parallel on top of each other without warning.
 Please note that the above mentioned options only apply to the internal of the structural region. They will not apply to edges and points on the boundary. In the case that the user also wants to prevent intersection on the boundary, he has to create the lines and points with the respective settings explicitly.
 Independently from the settings in XFLG it will always be possible to add single structural points and lines as constraining points and lines explicitly to the region using the command SARB
 CONS. Contrary to the default behaviour of SOFiMSHC, this allows to add only a selection of structural elements as constraints to a region.

The input table defines the parameter schema for **SARB-SLNB style boundary edges** used to describe one single edge of an outer boundary, inner boundary, or an inner constraint within a previously defined structural region at **SAR**. Each row specifies an **Item** (parameter name), a **Description**, an **expected Unit** (or “–”), and a **Default** value. Collectively, these fields tell the program what kind of boundary the edge represents, how it is geometrically referenced, and what structural properties (thickness, hinges, bedding, material) are applied along that boundary.

### TYPE (boundary category)
- **Default:** `OUT`
- Enumerated **LIT** values:
  - `OUT`: **outer boundary**
  - `IN`: **inner boundary** (e.g., openings)
  - `CONS`: **inner constraint** edges (used to represent constraining edges inside the region)

### NL, NP, NA, NE (geometric line/point references)
These govern how the boundary edge geometry is identified:
- **NL:** Number of a geometric line (**Default 0**)
- **NP:** Number of geometric points (**Default 0**)
- **NA:** Number of start point (**Default `*`**)
- **NE:** Number of end point (**Default `*`**)

A default of `*` indicates these are typically required/implicitly determined by the record sequence or linked geometry, while NL/NP default to 0 when not used.

### T (thickness in this boundary)
- **Default:** `*`
- **Unit:** `[Lit16/mm]1010` (thickness magnitude)
- Defines **thickness of the boundary edge/area portion**. In the surrounding context: thickness can be set on boundary edges to create a varying thickness distribution across the structural region (approximated via least squares between definition points/lines). If thickness is given on boundary edges, the region-wide general thickness at SAR must be explicitly set to 0.

### MNO (material on the boundary)
- **Default:** `0`
- **Unit:** `–`
- Material number assigned to the boundary. In general, material `MNO` can also support bedding definitions, including potentially non-linear bedding.

### FIX (hinge condition)
- **Default:** `-`
- **Unit:** `LIT`
- Specifies **hinge releases** at boundary edges using literals `PX, PY, PZ, MX, MY, MZ` (combinable). This defines which local degrees of freedom are released.

### DFIX (distance to boundary)
- **Default:** `0`
- **Unit:** `m`
- Adds a **gap** for automatically created internal edges when boundary conditions are applied, offsetting them slightly from the interior.

### CA, CL, CD (elastic bedding constants)
- **Default:** `0` for all three
- Units:
  - **CA:** `[kN/m^2]1096` axial bedding constant
  - **CL:** `[kN/m^2]1096` lateral bedding constant
  - **CD:** `[kN·m/m^2·rad]1099` (shown as `[kN/m/m/rad]1099`) torsional bedding constant
- These define **spring bedding behavior** at the boundary. The context specifies that the spring axial direction aligns with the edge’s local-x direction, and that `CL` applies to both local-y and local-z lateral directions.

### VAXI (variable-thickness axis ID)
- **Default:** `-`
- **Unit/Type:** `Lit4`
- **Purpose:** ID of the axis along which **variable thickness** is defined.
- The surrounding context clarifies that variable thickness along a boundary line uses **VAXI** and that the **name of the variable is given in parameter T as a literal**. This is intended for effects like a **bridge deck thickness varying along its longitudinal axis**.

### Overall interpretation
This table is essentially a **compact blueprint for a single boundary edge record**: it categorizes the edge (`TYPE`), locates it geometrically (`NL/NP/NA/NE`), optionally assigns structural thickness behavior (`T` and/or `VAXI`), and specifies boundary mechanics (`MNO`, `FIX`, `CA/CL/CD`, with optional interior offset via `DFIX`).

 This record describes one single edge of an outer or inner boundary of a preceding structural region defined at SAR. A valid structural region requires at least one closed loop of outer boundary edges but may also have a number of inner boundaries to describe openings or constraining edges. The edge can be given as reference to a structural line SLN or can be established directly by adding subsequent SLNB or SLNP records.
 In the case, that no outer boundary is explicitly given for a structural area, SOFiMSHC creates the edges on the boundary automatically on basis of the underlying geometric surface defini- tion, if one exists. This option is especially helpful when defining rotational (SARR) and free form surfaces (SARP).
 The edges of the boundaries can be entered in any sequence and orientation. SOFiMSHC sorts and connects the edges, provided that common end points exist and a closed sequence of edges can be found.
 Additional point or line constraints in the interior of the domain may be defined for supports, columns or other selected points using TYPE CONS. As SOFiMSHC however, automatically incorporates points and lines lying inside a region as constraint, there is usually no need for this option. Only in cases, where the automatic detection fails, it can be useful to add points or
 lines as constraints explicitly.
 For boundary edges and constraining points a thickness may be set at T in order to define a varying thickness distribution over the structural region. The thickness is approximated be- tween the given points and lines using a least squares method. Depending on the number of definition points linear and higher polynomial distributions of the thickness are possible. If the thickness is given at boundary edges, the general thickness of the region at SAR must be set explicitly to 0.
 Alternatively, it is possible to define the thickness along a boundary line as a variable along an axis, specified at parameter VAXI. In this case, the name of the variable is specified in parameter T, as a literal. This feature may be used to define a bridge deck, with a variable thickness distribution along its axis.

The table describes the parameter set of the **SARR** record (a property record) that defines the geometry of **rotational** or **sweep (swept) surfaces** for exactly one preceding structural area (**SAR**). It effectively turns a **structural line / geometric curve (GID1)** into a **surface** by either rotating it around an axis (**ROTA**) or sweeping it along a path (**SWEE**). If boundary edges are needed for openings or constraints, they are typically created automatically; only special cases require explicit **SARB** edge records.

### Field-by-field meaning

- **Item: Type**  
  Defines the surface construction method. Unit is not applicable.  
  Allowed values:  
  - **ROTA** = *Surface of revolution*  
  - **SWEEP** = *Sweep-surface*  
  Default: **ROTA**.  
  Conceptually, this controls whether **V** represents rotation angle (ROTA) or how the surface extends along the sweep/generator parameterization (SWEEP).

- **Item: GID1**  
  Identifier of the **first generating curve** (the curve to be transformed).  
  Unit: “— / L It4” (implementation-dependent type).  
  Default: `*` (required/variable; not fixed).  

- **Item: GID2**  
  Identifier of the **second generating curve** (trajectory/path for sweep).  
  Unit: `— / L It4`.  
  Default: `-` (not set), implying it is optional and mainly relevant for **SWEEP**. For **ROTA**, the axis is defined instead (via reference point and direction vector).

- **Items: X, Y, Z**  
  Define the **reference point** of the rotation axis (for ROTA) in the global coordinate system.  
  Unit: **meters [m]** (shown with “1001” index).  
  Defaults: **0.0** for each of X, Y, Z.

- **Items: NX, NY, NZ**  
  Define the **direction vector** of the rotation axis (for ROTA).  
  Unit: not specified (“—”).  
  Default: `*` (required/variable). This vector determines the axis orientation in space. For sweep surfaces, this may be used as an alternative to GID2 (trajectory vector), depending on how the system interprets the record.

- **Items: UMIN, UMAX**  
  Control the **extent in the u-direction**. Interpretation depends on Type:  
  - For **SWEEP**: extent along the **trajectory curve GID2** (or along the direction vector if a trajectory curve is not used).  
  - Also described as the extent along the generating movement for the swept/translated portion.  
  Unit: dimensionless (“—”). Default: `*` (use full available span).

- **Items: VMIN, VMAX**  
  Control the **extent in the v-direction** along the **generating curve GID1**.  
  Unit: **degrees [deg]** (as shown).  
  Default: **VMIN = 0.0**, **VMAX = `*`**. The documentation states that for rotational surfaces, if not given, the rotation angle defaults to **0 to 180 degrees**. It also warns against specifying full closed revolutions like 0–360°, recommending splitting into half-shells (e.g., 0–180 and 0–-180) to avoid ambiguity.

### Important geometric behavior (context)
When **Type = ROTA**, the system rotates curve **GID1** around the axis defined by **(X,Y,Z)** and **(NX,NY,NZ)**, producing a surface portion limited by **UMIN/UMAX** (along the generating curve parameter) and **VMIN/VMAX** (rotation angle).  
When **Type = SWEEP (SWEEP-surface)**, curve **GID1** is moved along **GID2** (trajectory) or along the given direction vector (**NX,NY,NZ**) and the extents are governed by **UMIN/UMAX**, while **VMIN/VMAX** still limits the generating curve portion.

Overall, the table provides the schema for controlling **which curves** are used (**GID1/GID2**) and **how the surface is spatially constructed and bounded** (**axis/trajectory reference and extents**).

See also: SAR
 SARR
 The given record SARR defines the geometry of rotational or sweep-surfaces. The record is a property record and refers to the directly preceding definition of a structural area SAR. Only one record SARR is allowed or each structural area.
 The following types of geometry can be described with this record:
 • ROTA: Surface of revolution A given structural line or geometric curve GID1 is rotated about a straight axis in space. The rotation axis is defined by a point at X,Y,Z and a direc- tionvector at NX,NY,NZ.
 The parameters UMIN and UMAX define the extends of the surface in meridian direction along the generating curve GID1. If nothing is given, the whole curve GID1 is taken. The extend of the rotation angle in degree is defined using the paramters VMIN and VMAX. If nothing is given, the parameters default to an angle from 0 to 180 degree.
 Important: In order to avoid ambiguity in numerical operations, surfaces of revolution should never be defined as closed surface with a rotation angle from eg. 0 to 360 degree. In these cases it is recommended to create two halfshells with angles from 0 to 180 degree and 0 to -180 degree respectively.
 A structural line or geometric curve GID1 is swept along a so called trajectory curve GID2. Instead of the trajectory curve, a direction vector can be given at NX,NY,NZ along which
 the generating curve GID1 is moved.
 The parameters UMIN and UMAX define the extend of the surface along the trajectory curve GID2 or the direction vector, respectively. If nothing is given here, the whole curve or the length of the direction vector is used.
 The parameters VMIN and VMAX define the extend of the surface along the generating curve GID1.
 In general cases, there is no need to define the boundary edges of the structural area explic- itly, when rotational or sweep surfaces are defined with this record. SOFiMSHC creates the edges automatically at the boundary of the geometry surface. Only in cases if openings or constraining edges should be defined or the boundary of the structural area does not coincide with the extends of the geometric surface, the boundary edges have to be defined explicitly using records of type SARB.

This table defines the **data structure/parameters for point records** used in **SARP** freeform surface geometry definitions (see also SAR, SARN, SARP). In this context, each SARP record represents **one point on a surface**. Typically, multiple points are provided in an **m × n grid-like pattern**, which later gets interpolated or used as control points to create the full surface.

The table has four columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**. Each row specifies a required or optional field name, what it means, its unit (if applicable), and the default value when not explicitly given.

### Fields

- **TYPE** (Type of data point)  
  - **Meaning:** Indicates the kind of point data representation being provided. This parameter determines how the given points are interpreted as part of the surface definition.
  - **Unit:** Listed as **“Lit”** (literature/identifier style), but no physical unit applies.
  - **Default:** **“-”** (no default shown; it is effectively a classification parameter).

- **M** (Position in u-direction {1,…})  
  - **Meaning:** Grid index locating the point along the **u-direction** of the surface parameterization.
  - **Unit:** None (dimensionless index).
  - **Default:** **“!”** marker indicates **mandatory/required**.

- **N** (Position in v-direction {1,…})  
  - **Meaning:** Grid index locating the point along the **v-direction** of the surface.
  - **Unit:** None (dimensionless index).
  - **Default:** **“!”** marker indicates **mandatory/required**.

- **X** (X-coordinate)  
  - **Meaning:** Cartesian **x** position of the surface point.
  - **Unit:** **[m]₁₀₀₁** (meters; unit system notation from the manual).
  - **Default:** **0.0**

- **Y** (Y-coordinate)  
  - **Meaning:** Cartesian **y** position of the surface point.
  - **Unit:** **[m]₁₀₀₁** (meters).
  - **Default:** **0.0**

- **Z** (Z-coordinate)  
  - **Meaning:** Cartesian **z** position of the surface point.
  - **Unit:** **[m]₁₀₀₁** (meters).
  - **Default:** **0.0**

- **W** (Weight of control-point, only for TYPE NURB)  
  - **Meaning:** Weight associated with a control point when defining a **NURBS surface**. This supports rational NURBS; weights typically influence curvature behavior. The surrounding context notes that for non-rational NURBS surfaces, weights can still be provided and may be set such that they do not change the interpretation (e.g., **W < > 1.0** in the text).
  - **Unit:** None (dimensionless scalar).
  - **Default:** **1.0**

- **T** (Thickness of plate at point; currently not supported)  
  - **Meaning:** Intended thickness value assigned at the grid point. However, the manual context explicitly states it is **currently not supported**.
  - **Unit:** **[mm]₁₀₁₀** (millimeters).
  - **Default:** **“-”** (no default indicated)

### How this table fits the SARP process
When using **SARP**, the software expects a set of points organized by their **M** and **N** indices. Depending on **TYPE**, these points are either:
- **Bicubic spline-interpolated** (requiring an m×n grid of data points), or
- Treated as **NURBS control points** (also in an m×n grid), where **W** provides per-control-point weights.

If freeform surface geometry is used, **boundary edges are generally auto-generated**; explicit boundary definitions (e.g., **SARB**) are only needed for openings, constraining edges, or when the structural boundary differs from the surface extents.

See also: SAR, SARN
 SARP
 With records of type SARP an arbitrary freeform surface geometry can be defined for a pre- ceding structural region at SAR. A single record SARP describes one point on the surface. The points will be usually given in a m x n-grid like pattern.
 Depending on the parameter TYPE, following types of surface geometries can be defined:
 The given data points will be interpolated by a bicubic spline surface. The points must be given in a m x n-grid like pattern.
 The given data points correspond to the control points of a NURBS surface. The points must be given in a m x n-grid like pattern. In order to describe non-rational NURBS-surfaces (e.g. rotational or spherical surfaces), each point can also be assigned a weight W < >1.0. Additional information about the definition of NURBS curves and surfaces can be found in chapter 2 of this manual.
 In general cases, there is no need to define the boundary edges of the structural area explic- itly, when a freeform surface geometry is defined with this record. SOFiMSHC creates the edges automatically at the boundary of the geometry surface. Only in cases if openings or constraining edges should be defined or the boundary of the structural area does not coincide with the extends of the geometric surface, the boundary edges have to be defined explicitly using records of type SARB.

See also: SAR
 SARC
 Item Description Unit Default TYPE Type of surface interpolation Lt BLIN
 SOFiMSHC allows to create curved structural areas only by definition of an outer boundary. In these cases - if the user has not explicitly defined the geometry of the area (SARR, SARP) - the surface geometry is interpolated from the pairwise opposite boundary curves (Coons-Patch or Gordon-Surfaces). With this record the type of this interpolation can be set:
 • BLIN: bilinear interpolation The surface geometry is defined by linear interpolation of oppo- site boundary curves
 • BCUB: bicubic interpolation A bicubic interpolation also considers the inclinations of the boundary cuves. This allows to define surfaces with smooth transitions between adjacent structural areas.
 SOFiMSHC automatically performs a linear interpolation of the boundary edges, if the edges are not lying within a plane and no surface geometry has been set explicitly. Thus, this record must only be given if a cubic interpolation is desired.
 In order to perform a Coons-Patch interpolation, at least three closed boundary edges must be given. If more than four edges are given, they will be joined conveniently.

This table specifies the parameters for an **SARS** record that defines **boundary conditions and couplings**—specifically the **support/bedding behavior** and **kinematic or elastic coupling** for the **most recently defined structural area (SAR)**. It is related to other coupling/boundary concepts such as **SAR** (structural area reference) and mentions **SLNS**; additionally, the heading references **SARS** (the record type being documented). The table is organized into columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**. Each *Item* corresponds to a keyword/parameter used in the input.

### Key fields and meanings

**REFT (Type of support / bedding)**  
- Unit: **LIT**  
- Default: **>FIX**  
This selects the coupling/support type:
- **>FIX**: Use **fixed supports** (i.e., constrained DOFs consistent with fixed support modeling).
- **>SAR**: Coupling with **another surface** (surface-to-surface or surface coupling to transmit constraints/behavior).

**REF (Number of the referred element)**  
- Unit: **—**  
- Default: **—**  
This indicates the **index/identifier of the referenced element** (used when a coupling requires pointing to another entity, such as the target element or surface depending on REFT).

**FIX (Support / kinematic coupling)**  
- Unit: **Lit28**  
- Default: **—**  
Defines the support behavior or **kinematic coupling** specification. The parameter likely maps to a predefined constraint pattern or coupling definition set within the software’s “Lit28” reference list.

**CA (Axial bedding)**  
- Unit: \([kN/m^3]_{1097}\)  
- Default: **0.0**  
Axial elastic foundation stiffness for bedding in the axial direction. A value of **0.0** means no axial bedding stiffness (no elastic foundation effect in axial direction).

**CL (Lateral (transverse) bedding)**  
- Unit: \([kN/m^3]_{1097}\)  
- Default: **0.0**  
Elastic foundation stiffness for bedding in the lateral/transverse direction. Also defaults to **0.0**.

**GRP (Group number of the support / coupling elements)**  
- Unit: **—**  
- Default: **—**  
Assigns the generated support/coupling elements to a **group**, enabling later selection, processing, or output control.

**MNO (Number of stress–strain curve / material)**  
- Unit: **—**  
- Default: **—**  
Links the support/coupling behavior to a specific **material model or stress–strain curve** definition, relevant if the coupling includes nonlinear constitutive behavior.

**RCTL (Control parameter for surface coupling)**  
- Unit: **—**  
- Default: **1**  
Controls mesh generation behavior for surface coupling:
- **0**: Generate mesh independent of the referred surface.
- **+1**: If possible, generate the **same mesh as** the referred surface.

Overall, the table provides a compact specification to control whether the SAR is treated as a **fixed support** or as an **elastic/kinematic coupling to another surface**, along with stiffness parameters (**CA**, **CL**), references to other entities (**REF**), and optional organizational/material controls (**GRP**, **MNO**, **RCTL**).

metadata.sections: 5.17 SARS – Support and coupling of structural areas

content:
If option FIX is specified at REFT and no reference surface is defined at REF, the resulting boundary conditions are those of a fixed support. In this case, there is the possibility to define an axial bedding perpendicular to the surface and a lateral bedding within the surface plane, using the parameters CA and CL or a material number or a work-law at MNO. If a work-law and a non-linear material are given with the same number in a project, the work-law takes prece- dence. This setting can be overwritten by entering a negative number in order to reference a material in this case. Alternatively, a fixed support can be defined by specifying the correspond- ing degrees of freedom using FIX. Local degrees of freedom (e.g. ’LPXPY’) are considered in the local coordinate system of the structural area. Rotational degrees of freedom are ignored.
 In contrast to parameters CB, CT of the structural area record SAR, which are processed as bedding constants during quad element generation, with this record spring elements with the corresponding constants are created. The properties of the spring elements are scaled according to their area of influence, in order to achieve a uniform bedding effect across the structural area. The spring elements, as well as the fixed supports, can be assigned to a group, regardless of the group of the structural area.

With the input of option >SAR at REFT and a number at REF, it is possible to couple two structural areas with each other, as in the following example:
 +PROG SOFIMSHC
 HEAD
 ...
 SAR 1 T 200 ... SARB OUT ... SARS REFT >SAR 2 CA 10000.0 CL 1000.0 ... END
 END
 In this example, structural area 1 is coupled with structural area 2 and an elastic bedding is generated between the two, with an axial stiffness of 10000.0 kN/m3 and a lateral stiffness of 1000.0 kN/m3. The bedding is modeled by means of individual spring elements between corresponding nodes, which are then scaled according to their area of influence.
 By default, if the geometry of the structural areas allows it, the resulting meshes of the coupled areas will have the same pattern of subdivision, so that every node of the generated mesh can be coupled with a node of the reference mesh. This behavior can be disabled with the use of parameter RCTL. In case that, due to the areas’ geometry or use of RCTL, such a correspondence does not exist for the two meshes, the kinematic coupling will be generated directly on the reference area, if necessary.

This table documents the fields of a record (referenced in the surrounding context as the definition of a *structural volume* that can be meshed into volumetric elements, particularly **unstructured tetrahedral elements**). It specifies how the volume is identified, how boundary conditions and material associations are applied, and which element type the mesher should generate. In the broader workflow, the volume geometry is defined by successive **SVOB** records, and the resulting tetrahedral mesh is a lower-quality alternative to structured hexahedral meshes (which can be generated in SOFiMSHA via quad-mesh extrusion/loft/interpolation). The record also notes that an unstructured tetrahedral mesh can alternatively be defined via **SOFIMSHA: UMSH**.

### Table structure
The table has columns:
- **Item**: field mnemonic/name.
- **Description**: meaning of the field.
- **Unit**: unit or allowed data domain (often “–” for none, or “LIT” for an integer/lookup identifier).
- **Default**: default value if the field is not specified.

### Fields
1. **NO** (Unit: – ; Default: `*`)
   - **Number of structural volume**.
   - This is the primary identifier of the volume. The default `*` indicates it is not optional and must be provided (or is required/defined by the program logic).

2. **FIX** (Unit: `LIT` ; Default: `*`)
   - **Boundary condition within the volume**.
   - `LIT` indicates a boundary-condition label or integer identifier.
   - Default `*` suggests it is mandatory.

3. **GRP** (Unit: – ; Default: `0`)
   - **Group number of volume elements**.
   - If unspecified, volume elements belong to group **0**.

4. **MNO** (Unit: – ; Default: `0`)
   - **Material number of volume elements**.
   - Default material assignment is **0**.

5. **MRF** (Unit: – ; Default: `0`)
   - **Material number of reinforcement** (relevant for reinforced material behavior).
   - Default is **0** (no reinforcement material defined).

6. **TYPE** (Unit: `LIT` ; Default: `TET`)
   - **Type of element** generated for the volume mesh.
   - Supported value shown:
     - **TET**: **Unstructured tetrahedral mesh**.
   - The default is `TET`, aligning with the context that tetrahedral quality is inferior to hexahedra.

7. **TITL** (Unit: `LIT` ; Default: `-`)
   - **Title of volume** (a label/identifier).
   - Default `-` implies no title provided.

### Implicit usage and relationship to context
This record defines *what* is to be meshed (the structural volume number), *how* it should be constrained (FIX), and *how* generated volume elements should be attributed to groups and materials (GRP, MNO, MRF). The **geometry** comes from subsequent **SVOB** records, while the **meshing approach** is tetrahedral by default via **TYPE = TET**; for alternative mesh strategies, the context points to SOFIMSHA records (e.g., UMSH for tetrahedra).

See also: SVOB
 SVO
 This record defines a structural volume, which can be meshed with volumetric elements (Tetra- hedrons). The geometry of the volume is defined by succeding records of type SVOB. By entering a negative number, the properties of an existing structural volume can be changed.
 This record allows to generate an unstructured mesh consisting of tetrahedral elements. The numerical quality of tetrahedrons however are inferior to hexahedral elements. A generation of a structured hexahedral mesh can be carried out within SOFiMSHA by extrusion, lofting and interpolation of 2D quad meshes. See records SOFIMSHA: EXTR, SOFIMSHA: LOFT, SOFIMSHA: BRIC for additional details.
 An unstructured tetrahedral mesh can also be defined using record SOFIMSHA: UMSH in SOFiMSHA. This records provides additional means to define the volume to be meshed and its enclosing surfaces.

This table documents a **property record** that defines the **boundary surfaces** of a **structural volume** within a larger modeling/meshing workflow. It is a “surface” specification associated with a structural volume identified by **SVO** (Structural Volume Object/Identifier, referenced as “the lastly defined structural volume at SVO”). The table also notes related concepts: **SVO** and **SVOB**, indicating this record works in conjunction with structural volume definitions (and likely their boundary/related records).

### Purpose and behavior
- The record defines **which surfaces bound a structural volume**.
- It is explicitly stated that for **unstructured meshing using tetrahedrons**, the specified surfaces must **form a closed shell** (i.e., the boundary surfaces collectively enclose the entire structural volume without gaps).
- As a property record, it does not itself define the volume geometry; instead, it **attaches boundary surface information** to the “lastly defined” structural volume context established elsewhere at **SVO**.

### Table structure
The table contains four columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**. Each row specifies a parameter required to describe the surface boundary.

1. **TYPE (Unit: LIT; Default: OUT)**
   - Meaning: *“Type of surface”*.
   - Enumerated value shown: **OUT**, meaning **Outer surface**.
   - Interpretation: This parameter distinguishes the surface’s role relative to the structural volume. With the only shown option being **OUT**, the record is intended to mark boundary faces that lie on the **external boundary** of the volume.

2. **NO (Unit: —; Default: ! )**
   - Meaning: *“Number of structural area SAR”*.
   - The description references **SAR** (likely Structural Area Record/Identifier).
   - Interpretation: This value indicates which **structural area(s)** are included as part of the boundary definition for the current structural volume. The unit is not applicable (denoted “—”), because it is an identifier/count rather than a physical measurement.
   - The default is shown as **!** (often implying “required” or “no default provided”), meaning the system expects a meaningful value to be supplied to identify the structural area(s).

### Key constraints for correct usage
- When used for **tetrahedral unstructured meshing**, the set of surfaces defined through such records must collectively ensure the structural volume is a **closed boundary shell**.
- The record’s configuration is context-dependent: it applies specifically to the structural volume **last defined at SVO**.

 Item Description Unit Default ID 128 bit code given as hexadecimal string Lt !
 This record allows to assign a Globally Unique Identifier to a structural element. A Globally Unique Identifier (GUID) is a worldwide unique reference number usually stored as 128-bit integer, which is primarily used for the unique identification of objects, when data is exchanged between different computer systems. It must be given at parameter ID as hexadecimal string, like for example:
 +PROG SOFIMSHC HEAD ... GUID ID '3F5A9ECC-145B-4093-9D16-E6F48732F569' ... END
 +PROG SOFIMSHC
 HEAD
 The GUID is a property record and must be given directly after the definition of the structural element at SPT, SLN, SAR, SVO, SLVL or TOWR. GUIDs will be assigned to all structural elements exported from SOFiPLUS or Autodesk Revit Structural. When describing the model using the CADINP language in text mode, it is usually not necessary to set a GUID.

The table describes **BBOX**, a record that defines a **rectangular 3D bounding box** used to select structural elements. The bounding box can be applied in two ways: (1) to select elements belonging to a **subsystem** (see **XSUB**), or (2) to serve as a **secondary group** in grouping/selection logic (see **GRP**). Conceptually, BBOX specifies a minimum and maximum coordinate in each axis, forming the opposite corners of an axis-aligned rectangular volume.

### Fields and meaning
The table has four columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**. The coordinate system is defined by six scalar parameters:

1. **XMIN** – *Minimum X coordinates*  
   - Unit: **[m]₍₁₀₀₁₎** (meters with a referenced scaling/format identifier)  
   - Default: **-1.e10**

2. **YMIN** – *Minimum Y coordinates*  
   - Unit: **[m]₍₁₀₀₁₎**  
   - Default: **-1.e10**

3. **ZMIN** – *Minimum Z coordinates*  
   - Unit: **[m]₍₁₀₀₁₎**  
   - Default: **-1.e10**

4. **XMAX** – *Maximum X coordinates*  
   - Unit: **[m]₍₁₀₀₁₎**  
   - Default: **1.e10**

5. **YMAX** – *Maximum Y coordinates*  
   - Unit: **[m]₍₁₀₀₁₎**  
   - Default: **1.e10**

6. **ZMAX** – *Maximum Z coordinates*  
   - Unit: **[m]₍₁₀₀₁₎**  
   - Default: **1.e10**

### Behavioral interpretation
An element is considered inside the BBOX selection region when its relevant coordinates fall within the inclusive ranges defined by:  
- **XMIN ≤ X ≤ XMAX**, **YMIN ≤ Y ≤ YMAX**, **ZMIN ≤ Z ≤ ZMAX**.  

The **default values** (-1.e10 for minima, 1.e10 for maxima) indicate an effectively “unbounded” box in each direction, so if the user does not override these values, the selection would cover a very large spatial domain.

### RAG/vector-store indexing considerations
To retrieve this correctly, queries may target terms like: “BBOX bounding box”, “selection volume”, “axis-aligned box”, “XMIN/YMIN/ZMIN, XMAX/YMAX/ZMAX”, “units meters [m]₍₁₀₀₁₎”, “used with XSUB or GRP”.

See also: XSUB, GRP
 BBOX
 This record defines as rectangular bounding box for the selection of structural elements. The record can be used for selecting the elements of a subsystem (see XSUB) or as secondary group (see GRP).

The table defines a data record for **storey levels** in a multi-storey building model. It establishes the vertical positions (elevations) and human-readable identifiers for each storey level. This record is part of a broader set of building/topology entities (see also **TOWR, GUID, XSUB, GRP**), where storey definitions are foundational for later structural layout and analysis.

### Axes and coordinate interpretation
- The **ZLVL** axis uses the **global coordinate system origin** as its reference point.
- The **ZLVL direction always points upwards**, i.e., it is aligned with the “up” direction opposite to gravity (as illustrated in the referenced figure 5.2).
- A key requirement (“Hint”) is that **gravity must be aligned with the global Z-axis** (either positive or negative) for the definition to be valid.
- Lateral storey extension (if applicable elsewhere) is tied to **global X and Y** directions, not the local gravity direction.

### Fields / Items in the record
The table contains two main data items (plus a control item) that drive system behavior and storey geometry:

1. **NO (Option control)**
   - **Purpose:** Controls whether storey levels are added/identified or removed.
   - **Accepted option shown:**  
     - `DEL` = **delete all levels** previously defined in the system.
   - **Unit:** none (`-`).
   - **Default:** `-` (no default action implied).

2. **ZLVL (Storey elevation)**
   - **Purpose:** Specifies the vertical location of a storey level.
   - **Sign convention:** **Upwards is positive** (“upwards positive”).
   - **Unit:** `[m]1006` (the unit format indicates the software’s internal scaling/precision convention; effectively a length in meters with a factor/encoding of 10^6).
   - **Default:** marked with `!`, meaning a value is required (no meaningful default is provided).

3. **TITL (Designation / label)**
   - **Purpose:** Provides the **text label** (designation) for the storey level, used for readability and identification.
   - **Unit:** `Lit32` (text length/encoding consistent with a 32-character limit).
   - **Default:** marked with `*`, implying a default or placeholder may be generated/allowed by the system, but the record supports explicit naming.

### Additional system behavior
- **Unique numbering:** The system automatically assigns a **unique number** to each storey level unless the user supplies one through the record logic (implied by “Storey levels will be automatically assigned a unique number, or it may be provided by the user.”).
- **Bulk deletion workflow:** If the literal **`DEL` is given at NO**, the system clears all previously defined storey levels, resetting the storey level set before new definitions are added.

### Relationship to broader modeling
Storey levels are used as the vertical reference framework for defining building organization and analysis. The table aligns with related entities such as towers and grouping constructs (TOWR, GUID, XSUB, GRP), and further guidance is referenced in the manual section on “Storey Analysis” for storeys and related functionality.

The image is a schematic cross-section/diagram illustrating the definition of storey levels in a multi-storey building. On the right side, a vertical Z-axis-like line is drawn with labeled horizontal tick marks and text “LVL 0 (base l…”, “LVL 1”, “LVL 2”, and “LVL 3” from bottom to top. Next to each tick mark there are corresponding height dimensions labeled “h1”, “h2”, and “h3” between successive storey level planes. An upward-pointing symbol near the axis indicates the positive direction of the Z-coordinate.

In the building interior, three stacked storeys are shown using thick horizontal beams/plates and vertical columns. For each storey, there are two vertical column lines (or column edges) and a horizontal shear-force line across the span. At each storey level, the horizontal elements are annotated with the text “Shear force” and small “+”-like blocks that visually indicate the shear-force application or internal shear hinge locations. The diagram is simplified in black linework with white background.

At the bottom, the base/support is depicted by hatched triangular shapes under the columns (two support regions), indicating fixed or bearing supports at the ground level. The mid-level (between LVL 1 and LVL 2) includes an internal dashed reference line that slopes, labeled “u” along the dashed line, suggesting displacement components. Another curved or arrow-like label “drift” appears between LVL 1 and LVL 2 region, indicating storey drift. The slanted dashed line suggests lateral deformation between the storey shear-force diagrams.

Overall, the figure emphasizes the relationship between storey levels (LVL 0–3), their associated elevations and vertical heights (h1–h3), and the internal shear-force representation at each level, all referenced to the global vertical coordinate system axis. The construction is clearly meant to communicate that storey boundaries are defined by horizontal planes at specified Z elevations, and that structural response measures like drift and displacement are evaluated per storey.

See also: TOWR, GUID, XSUB, GRP
 SLVL
 This record defines the storey levels for a multi-storey building. The ZLVL axis has its origin at the global coordinate system origin and always points upwards (opposed to gravity), see figure 5.2.
 Hint
 The definition of storey levels requires the gravity direction to be aligned with the global Z-coordinate axis (positive or negative); lateral storey extension is associated with global coordinates in X- and Y-direction.
 Storey levels will be automatically assigned a unique number, or it may be provided by the user. If the literal ’DEL’ is given at NO, all previously defined storey levels will be deleted from the system.
 For more information about storeys, towers and related functionality, please refer to Section

The input table documents the parameter set used to define a **TOWR** record in FEABENCH, i.e., a **tower**—a group of storeys that forms a structural unit within a multi-storey building for seismic response analysis. Towers enable multiple independent substructures to exist within the same global model, or to model mechanically independent parts of one structure as separate units.

The table has rows describing each item/parameter, including its **meaning**, **unit**, and **default** value.

### Parameters defined in the table

**1) ID (Identifier)**  
- **Type/role:** A **4-character literal** used to uniquely identify the tower.  
- **Unit:** `Lit4` (literal of length 4)  
- **Default:** `-` (no default; must be provided)

**2) ZBAS (Elevation of base)**  
- **Type/role:** Vertical coordinate for the **tower base elevation**, establishing where the tower starts in height.  
- **Unit:** meters `[m]` (`1006`)  
- **Default:** `!` (explicitly required; no valid numeric default)

**3) Bounding polygon in the XY-plane: X1…Y4 (lateral limits)**  
These parameters define the tower’s lateral footprint in the horizontal plane:

- **X1, Y1**: First vertex coordinates  
  - **Unit:** meters `[m]`  
  - **Defaults:** `-∞` for X1, `-∞` for Y1

- **X2, Y2**: Second vertex coordinates  
  - **Defaults:** `+∞` for X2, `-∞` for Y2  
  - Note: The convention (rectangle defined by diagonal) is described in the context text.

- **X3, Y3**: Third vertex coordinates  
  - **Defaults:** `+∞` for X3, `+∞` for Y3

- **X4, Y4**: Fourth vertex coordinates  
  - **Defaults:** `-∞` for X4, `+∞` for Y4

**Interpretation of defaults:** The use of `±∞` suggests that if these parameters are not set in a meaningful way, the tower may be treated as having no effective lateral restriction (or the system falls back to an “open” extent).

**4) WIDE (width-based alternative rectangle definition)**  
- **Type/role:** Provides a second way to define the bounding rectangle. The context states that if only **X1…Y2** are given, they can represent a diagonal, or you can define an edge with **X1…Y2** and a width via **WIDE**.  
- **Unit:** meters `[m]`  
- **Default:** `-` (no numeric default; effectively optional/conditional)

**5) TITL (Designation)**  
- **Type/role:** Human-readable label for the record (and in practice, it can be used to name the tower).  
- **Unit:** `Lit32`  
- **Default:** `*` (placeholder/auto behavior)

### Relationship to tower/storey structure (from the context)
A **TOWR** record defines the tower ID and base elevation, while the **tower’s total height is determined implicitly** by the **topmost associated storey level**. After the tower definition, **storey levels** (e.g., via `SLVL` and `ZLEV`) must follow to specify which storeys belong to the tower. Multiple towers can share storey elevations, and each tower’s storey levels are independent.

### Summary for RAG use
This table is essentially a schema for the **tower definition header**, specifying: (i) tower identity (ID), (ii) vertical placement (ZBAS), (iii) optional lateral extent via a polygon/rectangle (X1–Y4 and WIDE), and (iv) optional descriptive naming (TITL).

See also: SLVL, GUID
 TOWR
 This record can be used to define a tower, i.e. a collection of storeys, which belong to the same structural unit of a multi-storey building, in the context of seismic response analysis. The use of towers allows the existence of multiple independent structures within the same model, or the seismic assessment of mechanically independent parts of the same structure.
 The definition of a tower consists of an ID, given as a 4-character literal, and the elevation of its base, defined by parameter ZBAS. The height of a tower is implicitly defined by the topmost storey level that is associated with the tower. The lateral limits of a tower may be defined by a bounding polygon, using parameters X1...Y4. If only X1...Y2 are provided, then these points define the diagonal of a rectangular bounding box. It is also possible to define a rectangle by specifying an edge, using X1...Y2, and a width through the parameter WIDE.
 The storey levels associated with the tower must be defined right after the tower definition. Different towers may have storey levels at the same elevation. These storey levels are unique and independent of each other.
 Example:
 TOWR ID 'TLFT' ZBAS 0.0 X1 0 Y1 0 X2 10 Y2 0 $$ X3 10 Y3 10 X4 0 Y4 10 TITL 'Left Tower' SLVL ZLEV 3.0 TITL 'Left bottom' SLVL ZLEV 6.0 TITL 'Left middle' SLVL ZLEV 9.0 TITL 'Left top'
 TOWR ID 'TRGH' ZBAS 0.0 X1 15 Y1
 0 X2 25 Y2 10 TITL 'Right Tower'
 SLVL ZLEV 3.0 TITL 'Right bottom' SLVL ZLEV 6.0 TITL 'Right middle' SLVL ZLEV 9.0 TITL 'Right top'

0 X2 25 Y2 10 TITL 'Right Tower'. SLVL ZLEV 3.0 TITL 'Right bottom' SLVL ZLEV 6.0 TITL 'Right middle' SLVL ZLEV 9.0 TITL 'Right top'.
 For more information about storeys, towers and related functionality, please refer to Section Storey Analysis in the manual FEABENCH: storeys and to the online documentation.

The input table documents metadata fields used within **SRES (predefined Result Sets)**, which are mechanisms for defining *Result Sets with a predefined structure and properties* corresponding to a specific modeling entity or concept. In contrast to free-form RSETs (defined in SOFiMSHA), predefined RSET items are **auto-generated** based on the RSET type and its associated structural elements. The table specifically enumerates the available **record fields** that appear in an SRES definition/header and supports how those fields are specified.

### Table structure
- **Columns**
  1. **Item**: Field name/identifier within the SRES record.
  2. **Description**: Human-readable meaning and allowable content for that field.
  3. **Unit**: Measurement unit associated with the field value (if applicable).
  4. **Default**: Default value when the field is not provided.

### Rows and field meanings
1. **TYPE**
   - **Description**: “Type of predefined RSET”.
   - The table lists **possible values**, including at least:
     - **NONE** (a non-specific/empty type)
     - **BEAR** = “Elastic Bearing at Node”
   - **Unit**: *Lit4* (indicates an expected literal/format/encoding length/type for the field).
   - **Default**: **NONE**  
   This field defines which predefined result set template should be instantiated and therefore governs what auto-generated items will exist.

2. **ID**
   - **Description**: “Identifier”.
   - It functions as the identifier for the SRES instance or the generated result set.
   - **Unit**: *Lit4*.
   - **Default**: **-** (no default identifier is provided).
   This field is essential to distinguish one result set definition from another.

3. **TITL**
   - **Description**: “Designation”.
   - This is a human-readable title/label for the result set.
   - **Unit**: *Lit32*.
   - **Default**: **\*** (star), indicating a default/placeholder designation if not explicitly set.

### Contextual interpretation for RAG use
When creating a predefined SRES, the process is initiated by a **header record** that supplies **TYPE**, **ID**, and **TITL** (as described by this table). After the header, records for associated structural elements follow, and the predefined RSET ends automatically when a new command is issued or when an **empty SRES record** is used. This table therefore defines the key header-level parameters controlling the result set’s **template type**, **unique identification**, and **display designation**.

SRES
 With the use of SRES, it is possible to define Result Sets of predefined structure and proper- ties, which correspond to a specific modeling entity or concept. In contrast to the free structure of the RSETs, which can be defined in SOFiMSHA, the items of predefined RSETs are auto- matically generated, based on the type of the RSET, as well as the structural elements that are associated with it. The definition of a predefined RSET is initiated by a header record, which specifies the ID and type of the generated RSET, followed by the records of the asso- ciated structural elements. The termination of the RSET is done automatically, when a new command is issued, or by using an empty SRES record. Currently, the following types of predefined Result Sets are supported:

This predefined RSET can be used for sets of spring elements that act on a node, as in the common case of bridge bearings. A number of following SPTS records are expected after the SRES record, which correspond to the springs that act on different directions at the bear- ing. The individual springs are allowed to have either an axial or a rotational stiffness. The generated RSET contains one force and one displacement item per spring.
 Example:
 +PROG SOFIMSHC
 HEAD
 HEAD
 ...
 SPT NR 1 X 0 Y 0 Z 0 SRES TYPE 'BEAR' ID 'BR01' TITL 'Bearing at Node 1' SPTS TYPE 'CX' CP 1000 SPTS TYPE 'CY' CP 1000 SPTS TYPE 'CZ' CP 1000 SPTS TYPE 'CX' CM 1000 SPTS TYPE 'CY' CM 1000 SPTS TYPE 'CZ' CM 1000 ...
 END
 With the above input, an RSET of 12 items will be generated: 3 forces, 3 moments, 3 dis- placements and 3 rotations, referring to the support springs of Node 1, with respect to its local coordinate system.
